text: Page, date, official account, a real person. Four quick looks.
Step 3 is to look for another source. Which one counts?
The same post, forwarded by three other groups
Not a new source. Forwards copy each other, so ten copies are still one post. Look for a source that wrote it on its own.
The DOH's official page, an independent fact-checker, or your health worker
Yes! These checked the facts themselves. When two or more of them agree, you can trust the answer much more.
A comment under the post saying "legit, it worked for me!"
Comments can be written by anyone, even by the seller. One story is not proof.
Another source means a source that checked, not one more copy.
Checking a product with the FDA
Tap each step, in order.
1. Search the product name
Open the FDA Philippines online verification portal and type the product name exactly as it is written on the label.
2. Registered, or not?
If the product is registered, it appears in the list. If nothing comes up, a health claim on it is a red flag. Unregistered does not always mean dangerous, but do not trust its claims.
3. Read the note
A food supplement must say "No approved therapeutic claims". That means it is not medicine. It cannot cure diabetes or replace the medicine your doctor gave you.
4. Still unsure? Ask
Show the label to your health worker or pharmacist. Never stop or change your maintenance medicine without talking to your doctor.
Search, registered or not, read the note, ask. There you go!
Tita forwards the tea post to the GC. Which reply helps most?
"Tita, stop sharing fake news. How embarrassing!"
It may be true that the post is fake, but shaming makes people hide and stop listening. Tita shared out of love.
"Thank you for caring, Tita! I checked: this tea has no FDA registration. Let us ask Kuya Jun before Lola changes anything."
Yes! Warm first, then the facts, then a source and a next step. Kindness keeps your family listening.
"Okay 👍" and say nothing more
Kind, but Lola is still reading it. A gentle correction, with a source, is part of caring.
Warm, true, and with a source. That is the recipe.
Should you quote-share the fake post to warn everyone?
Yes, post it again with "FAKE!" on top
It often backfires. The fake spreads to more people, and many only see the post, not your warning.
Better: reply privately and share the correct information instead
Yes! A private, kind message is easier to hear. Then share the checked facts, not the fake.
Delete the chat so nobody sees it
It does not help. Others have seen it already, and the people who believed it are left without an answer.
Share the true thing, not the fake thing. Smart move!
Where to report
Tap each place. You do not have to report everything. These are here when you need them.
The platform's Report button
Use Report on the post or the page. It is quick, and it tells the platform to look at it.
Fact-checkers
Independent fact-checkers check viral claims. You can send them a post and read their answers.
The FDA, for illegal products
Tell the FDA Philippines about products that are not registered or that make false health claims.
The cybercrime hotline, for scams
If someone asked for money or tried to cheat your family, call the cybercrime hotline, 1326. Never send money to a "miracle cure" seller.
Your health worker
Ask the barangay health worker or the health center. They can also tell your neighbours the truth in person.
Five places to turn to. You are never alone with a scam.
Trust a forward only after you paused, checked who said it, and found another trusted source.
Kindness keeps your family listening. Thank the person first, then share the facts and a source.
When you are unsure, do not share. Ask your health worker instead.
The barangay health center, Monday morning
So much paperwork, Ara! The barangay just gave us a new AI helper. Can it do my whole job?
Kuya Jun is buried in forms. A new AI helper has arrived. Let us find out what it is good at, and what it is not.
Here we go! AI for the repeat jobs, people for the caring.
AI is a tool. People do the caring.

An AI helper is like a very fast calculator or photocopier. It is great at jobs that repeat: counting, sorting, copying, drafting and scheduling. It does not know your neighbours, it does not feel worry, and it cannot be blamed. Use it to save time, so you have more time for people.
The helper is fast. The caring is still ours.
Good for AI, or needs a person?
Good for AI
Needs a person
Count the boxes of vitamins in the stockroom
Good for AI: counting is the same job again and again.
Translate a dengue leaflet draft
Good for AI as a first draft. A person must still check it.
Comfort a worried mother at the door
Needs a person: comfort comes from someone who cares.
Decide whether a patient goes to the hospital today
Needs a person: a referral is a health decision with a name behind it.
Plan this week's home visits from a list
Good for AI: fitting names into days is a pattern job. Check the plan.
Visit Lolo Ben, who lives alone and feels low
Needs a person: being there is the care.
Repeat jobs to AI. Care and decisions to people.
AI's weak spots
Tap each tile to see where AI needs a person beside it.
Empathy
AI has no feelings. It can write kind words, but it does not care about you. A worried mother needs a person who listens.
Local context
AI does not know your barangay: who lives alone, which road floods, who needs a gentle word. People who live there do.
Judgement calls
When two things matter at once, or the facts are unclear, someone has to weigh them. AI can sound sure and still be wrong.
If something goes wrong, you cannot blame the tool. A health worker answers for their decisions. AI cannot.
Empathy, local context, judgement, accountability. People first.
The AI translates a health leaflet into Hiligaynon. Who checks it?
Nobody. The AI is fast, so it is surely right.
Fast does not mean right. A wrong word in a health leaflet can confuse or even harm someone. A person should check it.
A fluent speaker, before it is printed
Yes! This is "human in the loop": the AI drafts, and a person checks and decides before it goes out.
The people who read the leaflet, after it is printed
Too late. Once it is printed and handed out, mistakes are hard to fix. Check first.
Human in the loop: AI drafts, a person checks.
Jobs change more than they vanish

Looking back, most new tools changed jobs more than they ended them. Some tasks go to machines, new tasks appear, and people learn new skills. The skills that last are the human ones: caring, explaining, judging and checking. Keep learning, and ask your workplace how the tool will be used.
Do not worry too much. But do keep learning!
The AI helper made a wrong schedule, and two home visits were missed. Who is responsible?
The AI. It made the mistake.
A tool cannot be responsible. It does not know it was wrong, and it cannot fix anything or say sorry.
Nobody. These things happen with new tools.
Someone always is responsible. If nobody owns the mistake, nobody fixes it, and the missed families are left waiting.
The people who chose the tool and use it
Yes! The people who picked the tool, and the people who used it without checking, are responsible. That is why we check.
A person always answers for the work, even when AI helped.
Which task would you hand to AI first?
Counting and sorting records
Writing a first draft of a notice
Planning a schedule
None, I prefer to do it myself
Thank you! There is no wrong answer. All of these are good picks if you check the result. Next, you will run a whole busy day.
Trust AI with repeat drafts you can check, such as counting, sorting, scheduling and first drafts.
Keep people for care and decisions: comforting, local knowledge, judgement calls and health advice.
Someone must always be responsible. A person checks the AI before its work goes out.
Bea’s room, the night before the barangay health drive
I have to make the poster for the health drive, Ara! This AI tool makes pictures in seconds. Is it okay to just use them?
Bea needs a poster by morning. AI can help her make it fast. Let us find out how to make it honestly.
Here we go! Fast is fine. Honest is better.
Generative AI makes new things

Generative AI makes new pictures, words and voices. It learned the patterns from a huge number of examples made by people, then puts together something new that looks or sounds real. It does not understand what it makes, and it can sound sure and still be wrong. That is why a person must check it.
New pictures in seconds. But it only copies patterns.
Bea made the poster picture with AI. Should the poster say "Made with AI"?
No. If it looks good, nobody needs to know.
People can feel tricked when they find out later. A hidden AI picture can make them doubt the whole poster, even the true health facts.
Yes. A small label is honest and builds trust.
Yes! A label takes a second, and it tells people what they are looking at. Labelled AI content is easier to trust.
Only if someone asks.
Most people will never ask. The label should be there from the start, so everyone can see it.
Label what AI made. Honest and simple.
Bea likes a photo of her neighbour Mang Rey at the health center. Can she use it on the poster without asking?
Yes. The poster is for a good cause.
A good cause does not replace permission. It is his face, and he gets to decide where it goes.
No. Ask him first, and respect the answer.
Yes! Consent comes before using someone’s face or voice, even for a good cause. If he says no, pick another picture.
Yes, because the photo was taken in public.
Being photographed in a public place is not the same as agreeing to be on a poster. Always ask.
Face or voice? Ask first. Always.
Where AI art comes from
Tap each tile to see who is behind the picture.
It learned from artists
AI picture tools learned from enormous numbers of pictures, many made by real artists. Some of them never agreed to this, and they are still talking about what is fair.
Credit people
When you use an artist’s drawing, put their name on it. A credit line costs nothing, and it shows the work belongs to someone.
Ask first
Using someone’s drawing with their permission is respect. Using it without asking, or copying their style to pass it off as yours, is not.
Behind every picture there are people. Credit them.
Why fake doctor ads harm
Tap each tile to see how a fake doctor ad hurts people.
People trust the face
A doctor’s face and voice carry trust. An AI copy of a real doctor borrows that trust without asking, and it can fool even careful people.
They buy unproven products
